newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to accept nuclear plant bids.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to accept nuclear plant bids.

text.p: Turkey will accept bids for its first nuclear power plant tender until June 30, 1997, according to the tender terms outlined in the Official Gazette on Tuesday.

It said "well reputed and qualified companies are invited to submit sealed bids for furnishing of Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant" for either a 1,400-MegaWatt (MW) or 2,800 MW plant capacity, having units that each produce at least 600 MW.
Analysts predict the plant, to be located near the Mediterranean village of Akkuyu near Mersin port, will cost around $1.5 billion.
The gazette said the plant would be fully financed by the builder on a turn-key basis.
The tender results will be announced on June 30, 1997, when the state power utility TEAS would publicly open all bids and assess the best one, it said. It did not give other details.
